messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - High timeout rate for DNS healthchecks in region az-d (probe fleet). Signal: probe_latency_percentile_95 > 1200ms for last 5m. Affected routes: regional-router-azd, route53-healthcheck-azd. Link: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/1953456789 :rotating_light:
Sam Patel: seeing the alert. looks like probe pushers started queueing at 16:03 UTC. any correlation with the control-plane deploy? :eyes:
Mira Chen: no control-plane deploys in az-d at 16:00-16:10. I see a spike in retries from the probe workers to resolver nodes. digging into resolver logs now.
Leo Alvarez: I'm on infra. pulling resolver instance CPU/network at 16:00-16:08. running `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=resolver -c probe --since=20m` to get quick samples.
Jess Rivera: checking customer impact - alerting page shows increased 500s for hosted api in eu-west-2 via az-d. Not a total outage but request latency and some errors. Looks like some customers hitting conversational endpoints are timing out. Marking potential P1.
oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-348 by alerting. Severity: P1. Incident channel: #incidents-INC-2026-348.
Sam Patel: taking initial lead. Mira/Leo, if this is resolver network flapping we should failover probes to secondary region where possible and suppress noisy pages. Runbook step: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/dns/probe-latency.
Mira Chen: snapshot from resolver logs shows a burst of DNS SERVFAILs around 16:02 coming from a subset of edge resolvers (edge-resolver-azd-{3,7,9}). Suspect Route53 healthcheck misconfiguration?
Leo Alvarez: Route53 config looks okay. I see unusual SYN retransmits on eni-azd-2 with high tx drops. network team on call? @netops-team
Jess Rivera: raising customer comms draft. Customers affected: 5 tenants with routing through az-d. Draft: "We’re investigating increased latencies for API requests routed through AZ-D; degraded performance may be experienced. Engineers are working on mitigation." Any additions?
Sam Patel: good. Add that we’re implementing probe failover and will post ETA in 10m.
Mira Chen: trying targeted probe replay to confirm: `curl -v http://edge-resolver-azd-3/healthcheck` returns 504s intermittently. Also telemetry for probe heartbeats shows gaps starting 16:01:45.
Leo Alvarez: executing soft failover: updating probe routing policy to prefer az-c replicas for new checks. Command: `rbctl routes set-probe-preference --region az-d --fallback az-c`. Doing a staged rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
oncall-bot: Deploy job started: probe-failover-2026-03-15 by Sam Patel. Job: #348.
Sam Patel: rolling to 10% now. watching metrics dashboard.
Mira Chen: note — some probe telemetry isn't being emitted during the spike. our aggregation lambda shows N=30% fewer metrics points for az-d between 16:02-16:06. could be SAMPLING or exporter crash, check agent logs.
Leo Alvarez: confirmed exporter process restarts on edge-resolver-azd-9 around 16:03. OOM? logs show `oom_kill` for process `metrics-agent`. sending core dump to infra.
Jess Rivera: customer-impact update: 2 customers hit >95th latency threshold. Posting to status with mitigation notes.
Sam Patel: escalate to eng-sre for memory leak triage. @oncall-sre please join.
IncBot: Paging eng-sre oncall: @eng-sre (rotation).
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-348 acknowledged by Leo Alvarez at 16:08 UTC.
Leo Alvarez: taking ownership for mitigation. I’ll keep probe failover running and work on metrics agent restart loop. Next: spin new exporter container with memory limits, bump restart policy.
Mira Chen: running quick grep on code path — recent change in exporter v2.4 added cache of DNS responses. There’s a known issue with unbounded cache growth under high SERVFAIL rates. might be the root cause.
Sam Patel: good find. plan: keep failover to az-c for traffic, patch exporter to drop cache on SERVFAIL and redeploy, restart exporters in az-d once patched.
Jess Rivera: status update posted to customers. ETA 30m for full recovery estimate.
Leo Alvarez: replacing exporter container on edge-resolver-azd-9 with image `exporter:v2.4-fix-leak` on canary, will monitor memory. Command run: `kubectl set image deploy/edge-resolver-azd-9 exporter=exporter:v2.4-fix-leak --namespace infra`
Mira Chen: instrumentation caveat: until exporters are stable, telemetry will show gaps. ensure incident timeline notes missing telemetry as a cause for noisy alerts to avoid false positives later.
Sam Patel: handing off lead to Leo for actioning patch and stabilization. I’ll step down for next 30m. If escalation needed ping me. :hand:
Leo Alvarez: acknowledged. taking lead. updating incident log.
Jess Rivera: thanks everyone — I’ll continue customer comms and coordinate postmortem notes.
IncBot: Incident INC-2026-348 status: Mitigated (partial) — probe failover in place; exporters being patched. Updated at 16:20 UTC.
Sam Patel: closing virtual handoff — leaving notes in the incident doc with commands used and a list of affected customers.
Mira Chen: final note — recommend regulator for Route53 healthcheck to add heuristic suppression when exporter telemetry drops to avoid alert storms. filing a follow-up ticket. :memo:
Leo Alvarez: will follow up with infra PR to add OOM guard rails in exporter and memory usage alert thresholds.
Jess Rivera: posting final customer update: "Degraded performance has been reduced by rerouting healthchecks away from AZ-D. Full fix deployed to exporters; telemetry gaps observed during remediation. We will publish a postmortem in 48h." :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-348 archived as mitigated by Sam Patel at 16:35 UTC.
